transcript:
Header: 2026-10-27 | 11:30 AM PDT | Duration ~58m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Morales (Saturn Harbor), Maya Singh (Saturn Harbor), Roberto Diaz (Saturn Harbor), Aisha Thompson (Saturn Harbor), Samir Patel (Saturn Harbor)

Summary (auto): align on marketplace listing requirements and the on-prem connector packaging and test plan.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lena): okay everyone thanks for joining, uh let's start, I know we've got a packed list. quick roll call?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Evan): yep this is Evan, hey thanks Lena, Maya here as well and Roberto and Aisha and Samir from our side.
00:26 Speaker 1 (Lena): perfect, thanks. for context today's goal is to align on the cert checklist for marketplace listing and to nail down packaging options for your on-prem connector so you can ship a supported offer. Marcus and Priya from my side will handle the more technical bits.
00:41 Speaker 3 (Marcus): hey everyone, quick note — we'll be calling out some specific runtime assumptions, like support for persistent KV cache and optional GPU.
00:52 Speaker 4 (Maya): yeah curious about that — our environment is mixed, some customers on ARM fleets and some on AMD GPU hosts.
01:03 Speaker 3 (Marcus): okay noted, we'll cover build matrix.
01:09 Speaker 1 (Lena): Roberto can you kick off with your timeline and success criteria?
01:16 Speaker 5 (Roberto): sure, our immediate ask is two things: 1) certified listing in marketplace by end of Q4, and 2) a validated on-prem installer so enterprise customers can pull from our private registry and run in their air-gapped setups. success is a reproducible test matrix and an integration guide we can bundle.
01:37 Speaker 2 (Evan): and for business side we need clear metering so usage appears on marketplace billing — we don't want double-billing or unexpected chargebacks.
01:49 Speaker 3 (Marcus): important — Redwood supports marketplace hooks for metering via a usage endpoint; we need to detail required auth token exchange. are you planning to route billing through Saturn Harbor's marketplace account or through each customer?
02:03 Speaker 5 (Roberto): ideally through our marketplace listing with a SaaS meter, so customers see a single invoice from the marketplace.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Marcus): okay that maps well to our standard marketplace integration. we'll include sample webhook and metering payload in the checklist.
02:21 Speaker 4 (Maya): on the packaging side, what are your expectations? container images only, or also an OVA or packaged installer? some of our customers want a simple rpm/deb.
02:32 Speaker 6 (Priya): we typically support a few distribution formats: OCI container images for k8s, an installer tarball with a systemd unit for single-node, and an offline bundle for air-gapped. the cert process requires at least one reproducible offline bundle.
02:49 Speaker 4 (Maya): alright that helps, thanks.
02:55 Speaker 1 (Lena): security — Aisha, can you outline the SOC2/pen test expectations from your side?
03:03 Speaker 7 (Aisha): yeah so for customers in regulated verticals they'll request SOC2 type II and customer-specific attestations. from the marketplace side we need to provide: audit logs, an inventory of crypto usage (KMS/HSM), SSO integrations info (SAML/OIDC), and a list of network controls: IP allowlists, private link or VPC peering options.
03:25 Speaker 3 (Marcus): noted. Redwood offers a private connector pattern that uses customer-managed KMS and supports both SAML and OIDC. small caveat: some of our private deployment docs sometimes show 'Redwood dedicate' which the transcriber mis-reads, but technically it's Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private.
03:46 Speaker 7 (Aisha): ok on KMS — do you support BYOK or HSM-attested keys?
03:51 Speaker 3 (Marcus): BYOK with external KMS is supported, and our private builds can reference a cloud KMS endpoint. HSM attestation is on our roadmap; for now we provide audit logs for key usage.
04:06 Speaker 5 (Roberto): that should be fine, as long as we can prove separation of customer data.
04:11 Speaker 1 (Lena): let's go through certification steps: packaging, security artifacts, test harness, and marketplace metadata. Marcus — want to start with packaging requirements?
04:23 Speaker 3 (Marcus): yeah. first, image matrix: we need images for amd64 linux with GPU support and cpu-only; optional arm64 cpu-only. for GPU, please indicate which CUDA versions are supported in your images. we recommend glide paths for quantized models to avoid large GPU memory requirements.
04:43 Speaker 4 (Maya): our infra team uses CUDA 12 and some older customers still on 11.8 — can you support both?
04:52 Speaker 3 (Marcus): we can support multi-tag images: v1-cuda11.8, v1-cuda12 and a cpu-only v1-cpu. but building and testing arm64 with GPU is usually not required — arm64 will typically be cpu-only.
05:07 Speaker 6 (Priya): also note that our runtime needs to expose a readiness probe on 8081 and metrics on 9100 so the marketplace health checks can confirm service is up.
05:19 Speaker 5 (Roberto): got it. what's the expected startup time? some customers will fail certification if startup is > 90s.
05:27 Speaker 3 (Marcus): target cold-start under 45s for cpu-only, and under 20s for warm paths. we'll put the formal SLA targets in the doc.
05:35 Speaker 2 (Evan): on billing — if you're using the marketplace metering endpoint will Redwood validate event shapes or do we need to translate?
05:44 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Redwood will provide the event schema; we ask you to POST usage events with a signed token. we'll validate and surface invoices. note: we'll support delta and absolute usage, but recommend token rotation every 30 days.
05:58 Speaker 4 (Maya): sounds reasonable.
06:02 Speaker 1 (Lena): network models — some customers require VPC peering, others private link. Samir, what's common for Saturn Harbor customers?
06:11 Speaker 8 (Samir): we see both, but larger enterprise prefer VPC peering with strict CIDR ranges and strict egress rules. some smaller customers prefer site-to-site or an appliance.
06:22 Speaker 3 (Marcus): in that case we'll supply both patterns: peering with static IPs and an appliance mode using an offline bundle and registry mirror instructions.
06:33 Speaker 7 (Aisha): audit logs — how granular are the logs you provide? we need per-request logging with redaction options for PII.
06:43 Speaker 3 (Marcus): per-request trace IDs, request/response hashes, and token id. PII redaction is configurable; we can redact prompt content in logs if required.
06:54 Speaker 4 (Maya): ok excellent.
07:00 Speaker 5 (Roberto): certification tests — what does Redwood expect we run vs what you run?
07:06 Speaker 3 (Marcus): good question. Redwood will run the functional certification harness in your staging with you on the call. you'll run an initial self-test suite we provide which includes image verification, health-checks, and basic inference smoke tests. we'll run end-to-end metering and failover tests.
07:25 Speaker 6 (Priya): timeline: self-tests (week 1), joint pre-cert with Redwood (week 2), remediate (week 3), cert run (week 4). that's roughly a 4-week cadence.
07:36 Speaker 5 (Roberto): that fits our Q4 ask if we start ASAP.
07:41 Speaker 1 (Lena): great. let's talk about the marketplace listing assets — Roberto, you'll need an images list, short/long descriptions, logos, and a security questionnaire. the marketplace also wants a partner contact and support SLA.
07:56 Speaker 5 (Roberto): on logos — any guidelines?
07:58 Speaker 1 (Lena): yes we'll send the brand asset spec. avoid small text in logos and provide a transparent background png 1024x1024 and a vector svg.
08:10 Speaker 4 (Maya): one more on billing — will refunds or usage corrections be handled through the marketplace or direct between us and the customer?
08:19 Speaker 3 (Marcus): marketplace billing model typically handles charge and then partners reconcile with customers. we'll include notes about dispute workflows.
08:29 Speaker 7 (Aisha): we need to ensure compliance for EU customers — data residency and log retention.
08:36 Speaker 1 (Lena): Redwood supports region pinning for hosted inference but for on-prem you'll own residency. for logs we can provide retention config in the bundle.
08:46 Speaker 4 (Maya): perfect.
08:51 Speaker 2 (Evan): want to call out one risk: our legacy customers have strict kernel module blacklists preventing some container runtimes. any plan for a non-container path?
09:03 Speaker 6 (Priya): we can provide a tarball with a systemd service that uses runc or crun depending on environment; also an appliance OVA can be created if necessary.
09:15 Speaker 1 (Lena): let's surface docs on supported runtimes.
09:19 Speaker 3 (Marcus): yeah we'll add a compatibility matrix.
09:22 Speaker 5 (Roberto): testing infra — we can provide a staging cluster that mirrors our enterprise customer config; Maya will coordinate.
09:30 Speaker 4 (Maya): I'll provision and share kubeconfig to Marcus, but it will be behind an IP allowlist.
09:37 Speaker 3 (Marcus): fine — send CIDR and we'll use our IP for the test harness.
09:42 Speaker 7 (Aisha): small security nit — can you provide an attestation for the build process? we need to show reproducible builds for compliance.
09:51 Speaker 6 (Priya): we do provide build logs and image digests; we can sign images with cosign and share the public key. reproducible build attestation is something we can include in the cert artifact bundle.
10:05 Speaker 5 (Roberto): that works.
10:10 Speaker 1 (Lena): competitors — Evan you mentioned CloudWave, are they providing an appliance?
10:16 Speaker 2 (Evan): yeah they're pushing a fully managed appliance and marketplace listing; we want to differentiate by offering both managed and private connector models.
10:27 Speaker 3 (Marcus): okay we'll emphasize flexibility in the listing copy.
10:31 Speaker 4 (Maya): any blockers on Redwood side for supporting our air-gapped customers?
10:36 Speaker 3 (Marcus): none technical, main work is producing the offline bundle and documenting the mirror steps. our only ask is access to a staging env for validation.
10:45 Speaker 1 (Lena): great. let's go over concrete deliverables and owners — prioritized: packaging checklist, sample manifest, build matrix, pre-cert test plan, and brand assets.
10:58 Speaker 5 (Roberto): can you also share a sample marketplace listing draft? helps speed review.
11:05 Speaker 1 (Lena): yes I'll include a draft short/long description and bullet feature list.
11:10 Speaker 3 (Marcus): tech note: for the metering token exchange we recommend JWT signed by your platform; we'll show a sample flow in the doc. also we'll provide an SDK snippet for common languages.
11:24 Speaker 4 (Maya): thanks that's helpful.
11:27 Speaker 7 (Aisha): one more compliance question — do we need to include data deletion endpoints for GDPR?
11:33 Speaker 3 (Marcus): yes, include a PII deletion API and a policy for retention. we'll validate on cert run.
11:43 Speaker 6 (Priya): slight tangential — for model config what metadata do you want surfaced in the listing? model size, quantization, approximate latency per token?
11:55 Speaker 3 (Marcus): include model family, approximate vCPU/GPU requirements, quantization supported, expected tokens/sec and cost guidance. the marketplace page will show a small performance table.
12:09 Speaker 5 (Roberto): good.
12:12 Speaker 1 (Lena): okay to wrap — quick recap and next steps. Lena: send packaging checklist and listing draft by Friday 2026-10-29. Marcus: attempt ARM build and share logs by 2026-11-02. Maya: provide staging access by 2026-11-05. Aisha: confirm SOC2 scope by 2026-11-01. Schedule pre-cert run week of 2026-11-15.
12:40 Speaker 2 (Evan): thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
12:45 Speaker 5 (Roberto): thanks, we'll start internal alignment.
12:49 Speaker 1 (Lena): thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the checklist and sample manifests. bye.

Notes: transcription contains a few minor mis-hearings (e.g., 'Redwood dedicate' instead of Redwood Dedicated). References to docs: packaging checklist (link TBD), staging kubeconfig to be shared via secure transfer, marketplace brand spec (link TBD).
